1.init: comment one_euro~ - smoothing that keeps up
1.name: comment

2.name: text_block

0.name: block
0.value:
one_euro~ smooths a signal, and gets out of the way when it moves.

smooth~ is the same node.

IT CHOOSES PER SAMPLE:
Any fixed smoothing has to choose between passing jitter and lagging behind a gesture, because those are the same setting. This one does not choose once. At rest the cutoff drops to 'min cutoff' and the signal settles hard; as the signal moves, the cutoff opens in proportion to how fast it is moving, so a fast gesture arrives on time. It was designed for interactive motion data (Casiez and Roussel, 2012), which is what effort data is.

It is what you put between effort data and anything that will be heard - because control data that steps is audible as zippering, and control data that lags feels dead. After ramp~ it rounds the corners between one frame's move and the next.

SETTING IT:
Set the two controls in order. Hold still and lower 'min cutoff' until the resting signal stops shivering. Then move, and raise 'beta' until the movement stops feeling dragged. Setting beta first tends to end with both too high.

How fast the signal moves is measured in its own units per second, so the right beta depends on the range of the signal: a value that sweeps 0 to 1 in half a second is moving at 2.

SYNTAX:
one_euro~ [min cutoff] [beta]

EXAMPLE:
one_euro~ 1 1

INPUTS:

left in / right in:
The signal. With nothing patched to 'right in', the right outlet carries the smoothed left signal.

min cutoff:
The cutoff when nothing is moving, in Hz. Lower is calmer and slower to set off. Default 1.

beta:
How much movement opens the filter up. Default 1.

A signal patched to either of these is read once per audio block.

bypass:
Ticked, the signal passes through untouched.

OPTIONS:

speed cutoff:
How heavily the speed measurement itself is smoothed, in Hz. Default 1. It is smoothed so that noise cannot open the filter and let more of itself through.

reset:
Forget the history; the next sample starts it again.

OUTPUTS:

left out / right out:
The smoothed signal.

RELATED:
one_euro_filter is the same filter for ordinary per-frame data rather than ~ signals. Use it on a stream of values or lists; use one_euro~ once the data is a signal.
